prompt.text: Which of the following are consumers?

questions.explanation: Mushrooms are heterotrophic consumers/decomposers; algae, trees, and flowers are photosynthetic producers.

prompt.text: Which respiration process produces the most ATP?

options: They produce about the same amount of ATP
questions.explanation: Aerobic respiration yields far more ATP per glucose than anaerobic respiration or fermentation.

prompt.text: What is the net gain of ATP per glucose during glycolysis?

questions.explanation: Glycolysis nets 2 ATP per glucose (invests 2, produces 4).

prompt.text: A single molecule of glucose is broken down into ____ during glycolysis:

questions.explanation: Glycolysis splits one glucose into two pyruvate molecules.

prompt.text: The total product of glycolysis from a single glucose molecule (non-net) is:

questions.explanation: Gross (non-net) glycolysis products per glucose are 4 ATP and 2 NADH.

prompt.text: Place the molecules and processes in the correct order for cellular respiration.

questions.explanation: Order: glucose → glycolysis → pyruvate → pyruvate oxidation → Krebs cycle → oxidative phosphorylation.

prompt.text: Which is not a byproduct of aerobic respiration?

questions.explanation: Lactate is a fermentation product, not a normal byproduct of full aerobic respiration (which yields CO2, H2O, and ATP).

prompt.text: The rate-limiting step in glycolysis is:

options: The phosphorylation of fructose-6-phosphate by the enzyme PFK to create fructose-1,6-bisphosphate.
The splitting of glucose into two separate 3-carbon sugars.
The active transport of glucose into the cell.
The creation of 2 pyruvate molecules at the very end of the pathway.
questions.answer: The phosphorylation of fructose-6-phosphate by the enzyme PFK to create fructose-1,6-bisphosphate.
questions.explanation: Phosphofructokinase (PFK) phosphorylation of fructose-6-phosphate is the major rate-limiting control point of glycolysis.

prompt.text: One glucose molecule will eventually enable the Krebs cycle to turn __ times.

questions.explanation: Each glucose yields two acetyl-CoA, so the Krebs cycle turns twice per glucose.

prompt.text: Which reaction represents the rate-limiting step of the Krebs cycle?

options: The condensation of acetyl-CoA and oxaloacetate to form citrate.
The isomerization of citrate to isocitrate.
The oxidative decarboxylation of isocitrate to α-ketoglutarate.
The conversion of succinyl-CoA to succinate.
The oxidation of malate to oxaloacetate.
questions.answer: The oxidative decarboxylation of isocitrate to α-ketoglutarate.
questions.explanation: Isocitrate dehydrogenase (oxidative decarboxylation of isocitrate) is a key rate-limiting Krebs cycle step.

prompt.text: What is the net production of the Krebs cycle per molecule of glucose?

questions.explanation: Per glucose (two turns): about 6 NADH, 2 FADH2, 2 ATP (GTP), and 4 CO2 from the cycle itself.

prompt.text: The electron transport chain’s gradient is composed of what molecule?

questions.explanation: The ETC pumps H+ to create an electrochemical proton gradient used by ATP synthase.

prompt.text: Which is considered the oxidized molecule?

questions.explanation: NAD+ is the oxidized form; NADH is the reduced form.

prompt.text: Which process produces the most ATP?

questions.explanation: Oxidative phosphorylation (ETC + chemiosmosis) produces most of the ATP from glucose.

prompt.text: In anaerobic respiration, which of the following can serve as a final electron acceptor?

questions.explanation: Anaerobic respiration uses an inorganic final electron acceptor other than oxygen; sulfate is one common example (others include nitrate).

prompt.text: Which process does not make use of an electron transport chain?

questions.explanation: Fermentation regenerates NAD+ without an electron transport chain.

prompt.text: Which process occurs in cells whether or not oxygen is available?

questions.explanation: Glycolysis is anaerobic and occurs whether or not oxygen is available.
